newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium plans employee profit sharing scheme.
newsitem.headline: Belgium plans employee profit sharing scheme.

text.p: The Belgium government plans to set up a scheme which will permit profit sharing for company employees, Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Tuesday.
"A closer association of personnel to the results and the life of the company...is one of the government's priorities," he said in a speech at the Enterprise Foundation.

Maystadt said his cabinet was working on a draft law which will implement the profit sharing project via a cooperative firm, of which all employees of a particular company can become shareholders and whose aim will be the acquisition of shares in that company.
The cooperative will receive money from the company in relation to a parameter which measures the company's performance, such as profit or turnover.
Maystadt said the profit sharing scheme could in no way be seen as a substitute for workers' salaries and could not affect wage negotiations between unions and employers.
A Finance Ministry official told Reuters that employees would be allowed to buy shares of the cooperative for an amount of 22,000 francs per year and that that amount would be tax-deductible.
The cooperative's shares will have to be held for a fixed number of years, after which it will be possible to sell them free of capital gains tax.

She added that it had not yet been decided whether or to what extent the new scheme would be compatible with other schemes, such as the pension savings plan, which allows citizens to buy certificates of mutual funds for a tax-deductible amount of 22,000 francs per year.

In Belgium, some companies have been experimenting with profit sharing schemes for years, but they have often run into legal trouble with the tax authorities, who considered them as a way of paying salaries without paying taxes and social security contributions.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
